Pairs plot of the data with posterior draws of G ellipses

Source: R/plots.R
plot_G_ellipses.Rd

For each pair of traits, the lower triangle shows the data – or their residuals when X is given – with the level ellipses of a sample of posterior G draws (thin lines), the posterior mean G (thick line) and the covariance of those points (dashed), all centred on their mean. The upper triangle reports the posterior mean genetic correlation and its HPD interval.

Usage

plot_G_ellipses(
  fit,
  Y,
  trait_names = NULL,
  n_show = 100,
  level = 0.95,
  prob = 0.95,
  X = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A multivariate fit from lmm_animal (cmd_stan = TRUE) or a posterior draws object containing G and, when X is given, the fixed effects beta.

Y

Matrix of the observed traits (the Y given to the fit). Missing values are allowed: the ellipses are built from the pairs of traits that were measured together, and a point is drawn only for the individuals that have both traits of its panel.

trait_names

Optional trait names; default are the column names of Y.

n_show

Number of posterior draws of G to draw, at least 1.

level

Probability level of the ellipses, between 0 and 1.

prob

Probability mass of the HPD interval of the correlations.

X

Optional fixed-effects design matrix (the X given to the fit). When supplied, the traits are replaced by their residuals, Y - X %*% t(beta), using the posterior mean of beta, and P is the covariance of those residuals. Pass it whenever the model has covariates or factors.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

G and E describe the traits after the fixed effects, so with X = NULL the points and the dashed ellipse include the sex, age or group differences of the sample. Those effects can dwarf the residual covariance, leaving a cloud much wider than the ellipses; supplying X removes them and the scatter then has roughly the covariance P = G + E. Residuals are formed with the posterior mean of beta, so the points are those of a residual plot, not of an individual draw.
